chapter.title: What's Changed in ooSQLite 1.1
chapter.para: This chapter lists the changes made in ooSQLite 1.1, compared with ooSQLite 1.0.2.13107, the last version in the ooRexx Subversion repository on SourceForge (incubator/ooSQLite, revision 13111). It is meant both for programmers who use ooSQLite and for the ooRexx community, who may want to review what has been done.

ooSQLite was written by Mark Miesfeld. Its development continues in the GitHub repository JosepMariaBlasco/oosqlite, which contains the complete history imported from Subversion, so that every change described here can be traced to the commit that made it. Each change was made together with a test in the ooSQLite test suite; most bugs were first reproduced by a failing test, and then fixed.

In the rest of the book, the sections that are new in this release are marked &added11; and the sections that changed are marked &changed11;, as the ooRexx reference does. The embedded SQLite is version 3.52.0, as in ooSQLite 1.0.2.13107.

section.title: Changes That Can Affect Existing Programs
section.para: The changes in this section alter the behavior of ooSQLite in a way that an existing program could notice. In every case the old behavior was a bug: it either crashed the process, contradicted the documentation, or silently did something other than what was asked. They are listed first so that they can be reviewed before upgrading.

term.emphasis: Package functions and collations are registered under the name given

listitem.para: When createFunction was given an ooSQLFunction object from a package, or createCollation an ooSQLCollation object, the name argument was ignored: the function or collation was registered under the name it has in the package, and the method still returned OK. SQL that used the given name then failed with "no such function" or "no such collation sequence". For Rexx methods and for library handles the given name was always used.

Now the given name is used in every case. For createFunction, the countArgs argument is also used when it is given; when it is omitted, the number of arguments defined in the package is used, as before. Programs that passed the package name as name, which was the only way for them to work, are not affected. Registering a package with register, loadPackage, or the automatic registration methods still uses the names in the package.

SQLite identifies a function by its name and its number of arguments. Removing a Rexx function with createFunction(name, .nil) or oosqlCreateFunction(db, name) always asked SQLite to remove the function with 0 arguments, so a function with any other number of arguments stayed in place, while ooSQLite released the memory it used: SQLite was left with a dangling pointer.

Now the number of arguments can be given as the third argument, and then that function is removed. When it is omitted, all the Rexx functions with that name are removed, whatever their number of arguments.

term.emphasis: The authorizer callback gets empty strings, not missing arguments

listitem.para: SQLite passes NULL for the detail strings that do not apply to an action. The authorizer callback of setAuthorizer and oosqlSetAuthorizer did not check for that, so any SQL compiled with an authorizer in place crashed the process. Those arguments are now the empty string, as the documentation of the authorizerCallBack method already said. No working program can depend on the old behavior.

term.emphasis: An aggregate over no rows calls the final method with .nil

listitem.para: For an aggregate over no rows, SQLite calls the final callback without ever calling the step callback, and ooSQLite crashed. Now the final method, or routine, gets .nil as the aggregate object, as the step method does on its first invocation, and decides what the result of an empty aggregate is. See createFunction.

term.emphasis: More errors are reported in lastErrCode and lastErrMsg

listitem.para: The getFunction and getCollation methods of the ooSQLPackage class, and the autoFunction and autoCollation methods of the ooSQLExtensions class, failed for a name the package does not contain without setting the last error: lastErrCode was 0 and lastErrMsg "no error". They now set SQLITE_MISUSE and a message that names the function or collation, like the existing errors for a package that has no functions or collations at all.

term.emphasis: Errors from the final method of an aggregate name that method

listitem.para: When the final method of an aggregate implemented in Rexx returned nothing, or returned something that is not a whole number, the error raised named the step method instead. It now names the final method. Aggregates implemented with routines were not affected.

term.emphasis: ooSQLResult~blob and oosqlResultBlob accept Rexx data

listitem.para: blob of the ooSQLResult class and oosqlResultBlob only accepted a Pointer and a size. The classic oosqlValueBlob returns a Pointer, so the classic interface could pass a blob argument through, but the blob method of the ooSQLValue class returns a String, and Rexx code has no Pointer to its own data: a user defined function written with the object orientated interface could not return a blob at all.
Both now also accept a String, a Buffer, or a MutableBuffer, as bindBlob and oosqlBindBlob do, and the size is then optional. A Pointer and a size are still accepted, so existing code keeps working.

section.title: Crashes Fixed
section.para: Each of these bugs crashed the process with a segmentation fault (SIGSEGV). Each one is now covered by a test that reproduced the crash before the fix.

term.emphasis: Loaded libraries and packages and garbage collection

listitem.para: The tables where the ooSQLExtensions class keeps the libraries and packages it has loaded, and the tables where each ooSQLPackage and ooSQLLibrary object keeps its collations and functions, were referenced only from C structures, which the ooRexx garbage collector does not see. Once a collection had run, the next loadPackage, loadLibrary, or getPackage could crash. Any program that loaded a package or a library and kept running for a while was exposed.

term.emphasis: Functions with the same name and a different number of arguments

listitem.para: A function named f with 1 argument and one with 2 arguments are two different functions for SQLite, but ooSQLite kept the data of Rexx functions by name only. Defining the second one released the data of the first one while SQLite still used it.
Calling collationNeeded with .nil, to remove the handler, crashed. The classic oosqlCollationNeeded was not affected.

term.emphasis: The collation needed handler of a package that has none

listitem.para: collationNeeded accepts an ooSQLPackage object and registers the package's handler, but a package does not need to have one; with such a package the method crashed. It now returns MISUSE, as getCollationNeeded already reports an error in that case.
See above: any SQL compiled with an authorizer in place crashed.
See above: an aggregate implemented in Rexx crashed when it was evaluated over no rows.

The two routines were crossed twice, in ooSQLite.cls and in the table that registers the native routines; the two errors cancelled out, so they returned the right values. Both places are now correct. There is no change in behavior.

The sample code in examples/user.extensions, which is also used by the test suite, had three bugs, fixed in all the libraries: the ebcdic collation read past the end of equal strings, and crashed when a string was compared with itself; the reverse collation compared only the common part of two strings, so that "ab" and "abc" were equal; and the strAggregate aggregate failed with "out of memory" over no rows, where it now returns NULL, like the group_concat function of SQLite.

term.emphasis: Building with a modern C++ compiler

listitem.para: The register storage class, not allowed in C++17, was removed from ooSQLite and from the example extension libraries.

The syntax diagrams are now railroad diagrams generated from EBNF, like the ones of the ooRexx reference, instead of text. How to Read the Syntax Diagrams is the common section of the ooRexx books. The diagrams of the methods and routines that were still templates show their real arguments, taken from the code.
New section for a method that was not documented: collationNeeded of the ooSQLiteConnection class, with its callback method.
New or rewritten sections: createFunction, oosqlCreateFunction, createCollation, blob of the ooSQLResult class, and oosqlResultBlob.

Diagrams corrected: the count argument of oosqlBackupStep is optional; the user data argument of execCallBack is only present when exec was given one; traceCallBack was shown with the name of another method; attributes show a set form only when they can be set. The text of busyCallBack said that the user data argument was omitted when none was given; it is the .nil object.
The Rexx examples are highlighted, and errors in some of them were fixed, for example in the example of busyHandler.
Many sections are still templates. They are being written; meanwhile, their syntax diagrams are correct.

ooSQLite builds on Linux from a clone of the repository with make -f Makefile.lin, which was fixed to work outside the ooRexx build tree. The library needs the variant of APICommon from the ooRexx Subversion repository (incubator/APICommon), now included in the source tree.

The repository contains a test suite of more than 400 tests, written with ooRexxUnit, the framework of the ooRexx test suite. It covers the object orientated and the classic interfaces, the callbacks, the builtin extensions, and the loading of extension libraries and packages, with the test libraries in examples/user.extensions.
Every change is built and tested by continuous integration on Linux.
